ops.title: cc-squash cannot release: on a macOS runner the unpacked client has CS_HARD clear, so daemonkit's posture floor refuses the control lane
ops.description:
Blocking cc-squash's first release under daemonkit v0.23. `main` is correct and its fleet-build leg is green; only the release smoke test fails. Four tags — v0.12.0, v0.12.1, v0.12.2, v0.12.3 — are tagged and published nothing; their drafts are deleted and the changelog says so, and the tags remain because this repo forbids deleting one.

## The predicate, finally named

Three earlier failures masked it (broken isolation, a `/tmp` symlink in the program path, a missing `Library/LaunchAgents`). With those fixed the agent bootstraps and runs from the isolated root, and the daemon's own debug log — reachable only because this work added `CCS_LOG_LEVEL` — says:

    level=DEBUG msg="wire: reject connection"
    err="wire: verify peer: trust: untrusted peer:
         peer disables executable page protection (CS_HARD clear, status 0x22010001)"

Decoding `0x22010001`: `CS_SIGNED | CS_DYLD_PLATFORM | CS_RUNTIME | CS_VALID`. **Hardened runtime is set; CS_HARD (0x100) and CS_ENFORCEMENT (0x1000) are not.**

## What is ruled out, with evidence

- **Not the forbidden entitlements.** The release already fails on `disable-executable-page-protection`, `allow-unsigned-executable-memory`, `allow-jit`, `disable-library-validation`, `allow-dyld-environment-variables`, and `get-task-allow` (release.yml:196-207); that check passed.
- **Not the identity.** `Identifier=ccs`, `TeamIdentifier=SXKCTF23Q2`, `flags=0x10000(runtime)`, and the step asserts the identifier equals the binary name.
- **Not the signature shape.** `capt-hookd`, which passes this same floor in production, has the identical `flags=0x10000(runtime)` and team.
- **Not cc-squash's trust posture.** Every fleet consumer sets a signed `Trust.Control` — captain-hook, cc-interact, cc-orchestrate, cc-pool, cc-present, cc-review — and they work in production; captain-hook's control lane was exercised on both hosts on 2026-08-31 when `helper install` superseded it.
- **Not staging corruption.** Source and staged binaries are byte-identical by SHA-256.
- **Not `AllowUnprotected`.** In pre-v0.23 daemonkit that flag enabled a distinct same-UID `UnprotectedRole`; it did not waive posture for signed roles.

## The open question

Why does a Developer ID-signed, hardened, notarized `ccs`, run from a freshly unpacked tarball in a temp directory on a `macos` GitHub runner, execute without CS_HARD/CS_ENFORCEMENT — when the same posture passes for an installed binary in production? Candidates worth testing on the runner: quarantine or stapling state of the downloaded artifact, the universal-binary slice actually executed, and whether the bits are set at exec only for a validated-on-first-run image.

**Do not "fix" this by weakening `Trust.Control`.** The gate is doing exactly what it was designed to do; the earlier temptation to change it came from a log that could not name the predicate, which is now fixed.

## Second, independent defect in the same run

    [cc-squash] spawn proxy: exec: "ccs-proxy": executable file not found in $PATH

The daemon launchd starts has `PATH => /usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`, so it cannot find `ccs-proxy` beside the unpacked `ccs`. Decide whether the daemon should resolve the proxy next to its own executable rather than through `$PATH` — that is arguably a product bug, not a smoke-test one, since a Homebrew install happens to put both on `$PATH`.</body>

ops.text: Explain why a Developer ID-signed, hardened, notarized ccs run from an unpacked tarball on a macos runner reports CS_HARD clear (status 0x22010001) while the same posture passes in production
The release smoke test completes ensure/status/stop against the signed daemon, or the step is changed with a stated reason that does not weaken Trust.Control
cc-squash publishes a release; the tags v0.12.0-v0.12.3 that published nothing are recorded in the changelog
